rationale: Real, large spend and standard rep labor market, but extreme broker density, CHR/RXO consolidation and AI-enabled incumbents leave a newcomer mostly spot freight. Negative working capital (shippers 30-60 days, carriers quick-pay), $75k security, fraud/bad-debt tail. Base yr3-5 FCF ~$75-150k; early years founder is the book.
red_flags: New-entrant 12-18% margin is E, incumbents run ~13.5% AGP
Bond affordability depends on unknown personal credit

rationale: Strong access (households search, switch easily) and card-at-service cash flow; no license. But labor-limited, crowded with franchises and informal cleaners, discretionary in recession. Item 19 shows avg ~$431k sales/unit; owner profit at that scale likely $50-100k, so base FCF ~4.
red_flags: Labor 45-55% and contribution per clean are E
No operating-margin data for franchise or independent units

rationale: Mandated demand and prepaid tuition, low capital, but ~50 approved providers including national PE-backed online schools; Illinois-capped and housing-cyclical. Record's own ceiling is $10k/mo and yr3 $10-90k. Founder lacks broker/instructor license and needs licensed instructors.
red_flags: Broker headcount and new licensee volume MISSING

rationale: Producer license obtainable in weeks-months; buyers identifiable and statutorily motivated. But restaurant churn erodes book, liquor liability often E&S via wholesaler (split), new agency lacks direct appointments, and premiums/commissions are unverified. ~$1,500/account implies ~150-250 accounts for ~$100k.

Thin 15-25% gross margin, weekly payroll vs net-30/45, and catastrophic auto-liability tail; insurance availability for a new driver lessor is the unanswered gating fact. Driver supply scarce. Standard staffing roles delegate well, but yr3 range $0-150k signals weak base case.
red_flags: Insurance cost and IL WC rates MISSING

rationale: Broker margin layered on a ~5% maker residual; turnkey builds prepay components creating inventory/obsolescence risk; buyers anchored on cheap online Asian PCBA. Domestic quick-turn and harness niche is a weak wedge easily bypassed by going direct to EMS shops.

Contingency removes buyer cost and AI invoice classification is a durable edge; per-engagement fees can be large. But credibility wall vs CPA SALT practices, ERP data access, 6-18 month payout lag, denial risk and attorney need for contests. Base yr3-5 FCF ~$100-150k plausible, not proven.

Durable consumable demand with aging tailwind and autoship, but reseller economics are thin: ~$12-15/mo contribution and bulky shipping force CAC under ~$75 against Amazon, big brands and entrenched DTC specialists. Referral channel volume is hypothesis. Private label could lift margin later but MOQs and FDA duties unknown.

Real downtime-driven demand and searchable roadside buyers, cash often at service. But founder cannot do the work; each unit needs a $60-150k truck and a scarce senior diesel tech, so growth is tech-hiring-capped and key-person risk is high. Pricing and utilisation unverified; base per-truck profit ~$60-120k.
red_flags: Labor rates and ticket sizes unverified (E)

rationale: Urgency lowers price sensitivity, but must win approved-vendor slots before emergencies, demand is lumpy and auto-cycle exposed, 24/7 desk falls on founder early, and carriers want fast pay while plants pay net 30-60. No expedite market or margin data; 15-30% margins are assumption.

Low capital, prepaid seasonal plans and simple SOP labor, but five-month season, discretionary spend, pesticide scrutiny, and franchise plus lawn-care competition. Record's own ceiling ~$10k/mo; best as a line inside a lawn/pest route rather than a standalone holding-company base.

Mandated, recurring need; public establishment lists and in-person access; prepaid and very low capital. But low tickets, cheap online substitutes, restaurant churn and metro-bound classroom delivery cap absolute profit; record's own ceiling is $10k/mo. Tracking subscription willingness unproven.

Essential, sticky recurring commissions and books valued in M&A; A&H producer license obtainable in weeks. But relationship-locked buyers who switch only at renewal, PEO/payroll bundles, and a ~24-month ramp. ICHRA is a reasonable wedge. Commission PEPM levels are assumed, so FCF ~5 by yr5 is plausible, not shown.

Thin 22-30% GP staffing with payroll float, high competition, hospitals locked behind MSPs. Biggest issue: AI scheduling, intake, prior-auth and autonomous coding target exactly these roles, so 5-year demand durability is doubtful. Easy to start and delegate, little to defend.
red_flags: AI substitution risk acknowledged but unpriced

rationale: Record itself concedes no standalone wedge. ~20% modeled contribution after Amazon fees, ads and a volatile tariff stack, against Chinese direct sellers and distributor private labels; prepaid factory deposits and inventory risk. Abrasive safety liability adds tail risk.

Single-platform dependence with Amazon automating reimbursements; dozens of tools competing on price; no durable wedge (record admits). Low capital and easy access cannot offset fragile, shrinking recoverable pool. Record's ceiling $10k/mo.
red_flags: Recoverable pool after Amazon automation unknown

rationale: Brand economics are brutal even at scale (Laird Superfood negative operating margins on $34-50M revenue). Trade spend, slotting, deductions, co-packer MOQs and net-30-45 distributors mean multi-year losses typical; returns often realised only via brand sale. Hit-driven, not a reliable FCF base.

Thin 4-12% gross per unit on $20-80k units, freight-cycle price swings, inventory and floorplan needs credit history; dealer licence requires $50k bond, a lot with set hours and inspection. Judgment-heavy buying resists delegation; one bad unit erases months. Consignment-first limits capital but supply without track record is unproven.

Near-zero capital but low value per seat, offshore price competition, shrinking owner-operator pool and automated load matching commoditising the service. Serving multiple carriers with discretion risks unauthorised brokerage; segment associated with double-brokering. Record's ceiling ~$10k/mo.

Transaction-deadline demand, referral channel via inspectors/realtors, paid at closing, low capital, and IEMA licence obtainable in weeks-months. But volume of 200-500 systems/yr is assumed, competitor count unknown, demand tied to housing turnover; regional with modest adjacencies. Base ~$80-120k plausible.

Exhibitor prepayments and on-site rebooking are attractive, and a portfolio of shows can compound. But first edition is binary with venue deposits at risk, credibility wall before attendance is proven, recession and cancellation exposure. Emerald margins are mature-portfolio economics, not new-entrant.

Federally subsidised, lender-required, auto-renewing demand is highly resilient, but an outsider faces multi-generational farm relationships, consolidated agencies, rural presence needs, annual commission timing and a ~36-month ramp. Commission rates and crop certification requirements missing.

Two-sided marketplace needing $150k-$1M before liquidity; incumbent digital on-demand segment (PeopleReady) earned ~0.7% segment margin; workers multi-home; full DTLSA regime. Record itself rejects on structure. Venture-style burn, negative base-case ROIC.

Asset-light (~$20-35k), certifiable in weeks, standard technician roles, annual recurring scans for many identifiable plants; insurer referrals plausible. But NFPA 70B enforceability via AHJs/insurers is unverified, plants can self-scan with cheap cameras, and pricing is assumed. Full-utilisation $210k/tech is optimistic; base ~$100-150k by yr5.

No-risk shared-savings pitch and low capital, but fee share, terms and franchise economics are all MISSING. Generalist faces category brokers offering free audits and needs trust to open books; savings disputes common. Reasonable but undifferentiated without category depth.

Extreme Chicago roaster competition with quality parity, commodity green-coffee and tariff volatility, equipment and air-permit needs, net-30 wholesale. $2-5/lb wholesale contribution and record's ceiling ~$10k/mo make this a weak FCF base.

Buyers search actively and salvage supply accessible, but LKQ dominates, auction bidder competition raises vehicle costs, inventory-heavy, needs recycler licence plus zoned yard and environmental compliance; EV shift erodes engine/transmission parts. LKQ 7.3% op margin is incumbent economics.

Founder-hour-bound advisory in a field licensed customs brokers and attorneys own; classification/valuation work shades into licensed customs business and brokers cannot fee-share. IEEPA refunds flow via IOR/broker in CAPE and the window is closing. Transient, policy-dependent demand with no durable wedge.

Essential, prepaid recurring demand with waitlists in shortage areas, but $0.4-3M facility and pre-opening payroll at risk for ~10-20% mature margins, ratio-driven labor, heavy IDEC facility/staff regulation and director qualifications. ROIC ~5-25% by record's own math.

Asset-light, prepaid subscriptions, buyers identifiable from public bid tabs, and cheap-model crawl/classify is a real durable cost edge. But national aggregators already sell this, small-contractor willingness to pay is unverified, and Illinois-only TAM at $50-300/mo caps profit; multi-state means head-on competition.

Identifiable agency buyers with a real labor-cost pain, low capital, standard BPO management roles and repeatable pods. But crowded offshore BPO field, ~$500-1,000/FTE-month margin, and AI agents for COIs/endorsements may let agencies self-serve, compressing the FTE model within a few years.

Mandate-driven recurring per-hire flow and white-label platforms make launch cheap, AI helps verification. But scale CRAs win on price and integrations, ATS switching friction, FCRA class-action tail, and unresolved Illinois PI Act licensing (3-yr experience) could block or force a licensed partner.
